sufficiency.nextGate: Approve the content model for rendering

technicalJudgment.statement: Approve the solution shape with the catalog and BTP conditions explicitly gated before Build.

systems.name: Salesforce Sales and Service Cloud
systems.description: System of engagement for customer and case context.

systems.name: Revenue Cloud Advanced and Billing
systems.description: Contract lifecycle and billing schedule system.
responsibilities: Quote, contract, amend, renew, billing schedule

systems.name: SAP BTP Integration Suite
systems.description: Integration seam for all net-new Salesforce to SAP exchanges.

systems.name: SAP ECC and RAR
systems.description: Financial system of record for orders, invoices, revenue recognition, and GL.
responsibilities: Sales order, invoice, revenue recognition, general ledger

interfaces.name: New order transmission
interfaces.description: Revenue Cloud sends an accepted quote and contract to SAP through BTP.

failurePaths.behavior: Persist failed event, retry with backoff, then route to dead-letter queue without creating duplicate orders
failurePaths.escalation: Alert integration support and block downstream billing

interfaces.name: Billing schedule synchronization
interfaces.description: Revenue Cloud sends governed billing events through BTP to SAP invoicing and RAR.
interfaces.purpose: Synchronize billing schedule and modification events
interfaces.trigger: RCB billing event or contract amendment

failurePaths.condition: SAP rejects billing event or allocation data
failurePaths.behavior: Hold the event, prevent invoice progression, and route to finance review

adrs.name: Use SAP BTP for net-new integrations
adrs.description: BTP aligns the solution to the S/4HANA direction while existing Boomi flows remain.
adrs.question: BTP or Boomi for the new integration surface?
adrs.decision: Use SAP BTP for all net-new flows.
adrs.rationale: Avoid rebuilding the new integration during the S/4HANA transition.
adrs.owner: Apex IT and Estate Technical Architect

adrs.name: Revenue Cloud owns billing schedules
adrs.description: RCB manages schedule logic while SAP owns invoicing and revenue recognition.
adrs.question: Should billing schedules live in Salesforce or SAP custom logic?
adrs.decision: Use Revenue Cloud Billing for schedule logic.
adrs.rationale: Keeps subscription configuration in Salesforce and avoids custom SAP schedule logic.
adrs.owner: Apex Finance and Estate Solution Architect

scopeItems.name: Subscription lifecycle
scopeItems.description: Configure quote, contract, amend, renew, suspend, and cancel for Grid.
acceptanceCriteria: One contract supports amendment and renewal without spawning duplicate contracts

scopeItems.name: BTP integration flows
scopeItems.description: Design and build the order and billing event interfaces.
acceptanceCriteria: E2E order and billing scenarios pass with observable failure handling

scopeItems.name: Billing schedules and modifications
scopeItems.description: Configure billing triggers, proration, free months, and credit behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Billing schedules match approved scenarios and SAP acknowledgments

scopeItems.name: Salesforce-native revenue recognition
scopeItems.description: RightRev implementation is excluded because SAP RAR remains the revenue-recognition engine.

risks.name: BTP delivery experience
risks.description: Neither team has demonstrated the full target iFlow shape.
mitigationActions: Run a two-week BTP architecture spike
risks.residualExposure: Timeline and staffing remain exposed until the spike passes

risks.name: Catalog rationalization delay
risks.description: Material-number mapping may not be ready before configuration begins.
mitigationActions: Gate Design exit on signed catalog mapping
risks.trigger: Catalog mapping incomplete at Design gate
risks.residualExposure: Configuration and integration mapping cannot proceed

assumptions.name: SAP owns invoicing
assumptions.description: Invoicing, AR, collections, tax, and revenue recognition stay in SAP.
assumptions.consequenceIfFalse: Reopen the architecture and price a materially larger engagement.
assumptions.closureCondition: Finance approves the invoicing boundary at Design gate

assumptions.name: Apex provides a client-side PM
assumptions.description: Estate PM effort assumes an empowered client project owner.
assumptions.consequenceIfFalse: Increase PM allocation and commercial baseline.
assumptions.closureCondition: Name and commit the client PM before Mobilize

dependencies.name: Approved catalog mapping
dependencies.description: Material numbers must map to Salesforce products before design can close.
dependencies.closureCondition: Signed catalog mapping and data-quality checklist

roles.name: Solution Architect
roles.description: Owns Revenue Cloud lifecycle, billing boundaries, and technical judgment.

roles.name: Technical Architect
roles.description: Owns BTP topology, interface contracts, security, and failure behavior.

roles.name: BTP Developer
roles.description: Builds and tests the load-bearing integration flows.

roles.name: Project Manager
roles.description: Owns gates, decisions, dependencies, and delivery coordination.

allocations.name: SA in Analyze
allocations.description: Solution Architect confirms lifecycle and billing requirements.

allocations.name: SA in Design
allocations.description: Solution Architect owns system boundary and billing ADRs.

allocations.name: TA in Design
allocations.description: Technical Architect owns interface contracts and failure design.

allocations.name: BTP developer in Build
allocations.description: Developer builds and validates the integration flows.

allocations.name: PM in Build
allocations.description: Project Manager owns Build and validation governance.

phases.name: Analyze
phases.description: Confirm process, source data, catalog, and interface needs.
phases.objective: Turn quoted scope into an evidence-backed baseline.
exitCriteria: Scope, catalog approach, and interface inventory approved

phases.name: Design
phases.description: Approve architecture, ADRs, interface contracts, failure behavior, and acceptance criteria.
phases.objective: Make the system and delivery logic buildable.
exitCriteria: Architecture, interface contracts, catalog mapping, and test approach approved

phases.name: Build and Validate
phases.description: Configure Revenue Cloud, build BTP flows, and prove E2E scenarios.
phases.objective: Deliver and validate the approved scope.
exitCriteria: E2E happy and failure paths pass acceptance criteria

milestones.name: Design approval gate
milestones.description: Architecture, interface, catalog, and test decisions approved.

milestones.name: Validation exit
milestones.description: All E2E scenarios and failure paths pass.

financialLines.name: BTP integration services
financialLines.description: Priced baseline for interface design and build.

financialLines.name: Billing configuration services
financialLines.description: Priced baseline for billing schedules and modifications.

financialLines.name: Project management allocation
financialLines.description: PM cost is included across the priced scope lines.

reconciliationControls.name: Included scope pricing
reconciliationControls.description: All included scope items map to included financial lines.

reconciliationControls.name: Investment total
reconciliationControls.description: Included scope lines reconcile to the total investment.

reconciliationControls.name: Excluded scope contributes zero
reconciliationControls.description: Excluded RightRev work has no baseline contribution.

editorialViews.audienceTask: Know whether the solution is technically deliverable and under which conditions.
Understand systems, ownership, scope, and access boundaries.
Trace load-bearing exchanges and failure behavior.
Know what was decided, why, and what each decision governs.
Trace included and excluded scope to the solution and phases.
See where risks and conditions attach to the architecture and timeline.
Understand technical ownership, allocations, peaks, and feasibility.
Understand phases, entry and exit criteria, and decision gates.
Verify scope, staffing, timing, and investment coherence.
Know which conditions block progress and the next evidence gate.
